Hi Peter — appreciated the chat. Below is a concrete breakdown and two commercial paths we typically use for customers who want to go through a cloud marketplace but keep near-identical economics to a direct contract.

1) Marketplace (AWS/GCP) purchase — standard flow - Redwood lists our Hosted API on the marketplace. AWS invoices Acme and remits to Redwood. Marketplace fees reduce the gross amount Redwood receives (typical marketplace fee 6–12% depending on agreement). - Effect on discounts: list discounts we publish apply at the seller invoice level; because AWS takes a fee, the net received by Redwood is lower. We can offer the same public discount tiers but must account for the fee. Practically, we do one of two things (see options below).

2) Direct (invoice from Redwood) — standard flow - Acme signs a direct commitment with Redwood and we invoice monthly/quarterly. No marketplace fee, so list discount flows directly. This is the cleanest economically but requires Acme to accept direct invoicing and (if needed) Redwood to provide required procurement paperwork.

Two common commercial solutions to equalize economics:
A) Marketplace-side pass-through pricing (recommended when procurement requires marketplace billing)
- We publish a slightly higher list price on the marketplace to offset the AWS fee and map commit tiers so that the net-to-Acme matches the direct net price.
- Pros: preserves AWS invoice flow for Acme; Cons: extra accounting and we need marketplace listing updates and marketplace marketplace partner approvals.

B) Commitment rebate / credit (recommended when speed to PO matters)
- Acme purchases via the marketplace at listed marketplace prices. Redwood issues a monthly rebate/credit (applied as future usage credit or invoice credit) equal to the marketplace fee delta so the net economics match the direct price.
- Pros: fast to implement; Cons: requires clear SOW language for credits and internal reconciliation.

Example (illustrative):
- Listed direct price: $0.20 per 1k tokens at 1M tokens/month commit (tier 1)
- AWS marketplace fee: 8%
- Marketplace listed price (option A): $0.217 per 1k tokens — net to Redwood after 8% fee ≈ $0.20
- Option B: Acme pays $0.217 on AWS invoice; Redwood issues $0.017 per 1k token monthly credit back to Acme as part of the commit reconciliation.

Attached: Draft_SOW_and_Commit_Tiers.pdf (high-level SOW language we can adapt for Acme).

If that makes sense, Kimberly/Karthik — can we agree on which option Acme prefers and I’ll generate the DocuSign? Peter — which procurement path does your team prefer (marketplace invoice vs direct)?

Thanks,

Peter — adding the token math and operational notes (keeping it short):

Assumptions from ACME matrix: 1,000,000 tokens/month (steady-state)
- Direct list price (example): $0.20 / 1k tokens => monthly gross invoice = $200
- AWS marketplace fee: 8% => AWS invoices Acme $200, sends Redwood $184 (approx)

Option A — pass-through list price on marketplace:
- Set marketplace list price = $0.20 / (1 - 0.08) = $0.21739 / 1k tokens
- Acme pays $217.39; AWS fee ~8% -> Redwood receives ≈ $200 (same as direct)
- Notes: Need marketplace listing update and acceptance; price is visible on AWS listing so Acme will see the higher per-token price on AWS invoice (but net economics are equal after the pass-through adjustment).

Option B — credit/rebate workflow:
- Acme pays $200 on the AWS invoice (marketplace list price $0.217 => invoice ≈ $217.39). Redwood issues monthly credit of ~$17.39 to offset marketplace fee.
- Reconciliation: credits can be applied as usage credits or as a post-billing credit. We recommend credits be formalized in the SOW: "Redwood will issue monthly usage credits equal to marketplace fees for the committed tiers."

Other considerations:
- Taxes: marketplace invoices may change VAT/withholding treatment. Acme procurement should confirm with their tax team.
- Reporting: Acme will have AWS line-items; if they need a Redwood-stamped invoice for internal chargeback, we can provide a supplementary invoice showing net payment and credits applied.
- Contractual SLAs: marketplace purchases typically still allow for Redwood SLAs, but we should document in the SOW and support flow how incidents and credits are handled.

Recommendation: If procurement absolutely needs marketplace billing, choose Option B for speed (we can start the POC fast) and formalize monthly credit mechanics in the SOW. If Acme prefers pricing clarity on the AWS invoice itself, use Option A but be prepared for the marketplace listing update window (~2–4 business days minimum).

I’ll draft the exact per-token values for the three commit tiers you supplied in the matrix and share a final DocuSign quote once Kimberly/Marissa confirm the preferred path.

—Karthik
